bio: I tinker with hardware, write software, and occasionally share what I learn on my blog. Right now I'm especially interested in IoT, calculator hacking, and full-stack web development.
When I'm not coding, you can probably find me exploring new tech, working on side projects, or diving deep into some obscure rabbit hole.

body: My first time in the States was a summer coding camp at Berkeley in 2019, when I was twelve. What stuck was not the curriculum — it was how kind and encouraging the teachers and other kids were, a world away from the sterner classrooms I grew up with. I decided more or less on the spot that this was where I wanted to end up.
Seven years later, it worked out. I start at Cal in Fall 2026 in the College of Letters & Science, headed toward philosophy and business.
Outside class: chess, piano, and the bouldering gym two minutes from my apartment.
Three years in the Connecticut countryside — Class of 2026, GPA 4.14. The record, in list form:
Leadership — Chess Club president · founded the Badminton Club · founded the Robotics Club · ran a peer math-tutoring study hall (11 of 13 previously failing freshmen passed Algebra 1)
Math — USAMO qualifier, 2026 (AIME 12/15 · AMC 12: 138) · multivariable calculus by senior year
Humanities — John Locke Essay Competition, philosophy shortlist (2025) · National Merit Semifinalist, perfect PSAT (2025)
Sciences — AAPT Physics Bowl, top 10% (2025) · Yale Physics Olympiad team, the only underclassman on it
Music — First place, NY Golden Classical Music Award, piano (2024)
Athletics — Varsity crew, stroke seat · Founders League Regatta champions
Chess, outside school — ~2140 USCF · 5th place, Boston Chess Congress (2023)
